articles.title: The Uprising review – the peasants are revolting in muddled historical epic
articles.summary: Andrew Garfield’s charisma can’t save Paul Greengrass’s grim and depressingly generic period piece. Hollywood loves giving young actors their own historical epic as much as audiences seem to dislike watching them.
body: On paper, The Uprising should be different: it’s a historical epic from a blue-chip director (the Bourne trilogy’s Paul Greengrass ), a nuanced, introspective leading man ( Andrew Garfield ) and a milieu that uncomfortably chimes with the western world’s backslide into repressive authoritarianism (The Peasants’ Revolt of 1381). In reality, it is a disjointed slog through the mud with the emotional depth of a History Channel rerun.

Thus follows a rather hectic-feeling race from one greige setting to the next as the rebels have their run of modern-day Kent, assembling in Maidstone before storming Canterbury cathedral, and then traveling to meet the king and his men in Blackheath. Greengrass’s camerawork can occasionally swoon, with stunning aerial shots of a flotilla on the Thames, but his signature handheld style is a trick that has gone stale: the only uprising I felt during the seasick fight scenes was my breakfast threatening to return on me.
points: Andrew Garfield’s charisma can’t save Paul Greengrass’s grim and depressingly generic period piece.
Hollywood loves giving young actors their own historical epic as much as audiences seem to dislike watching them.

articles.title: Call My Agent! The Movie review – the gang get back together and c’est formidable
articles.summary: The screwball French comedy is back as a film that actually works, thanks to putting Andréa and Noémie at the heart of chaotic events and bringing all the old faces back. At last: a beloved-TV-show-to-film-spinoff that doesn’t suck!
body: Like many great sitcoms, this one always understood that failure, rather than success, keeps the wider narrative arc more interesting and relatable. So the last episode of the series left the gang at talent agency ASK (which stood for Agence Samuel Kerr, after the founder, who died in the first episode), dispersed to new gigs and careers; the band, in effect, broke up. Five years on, the stars have aligned to bring them all back together to work on Andréa (Cottin) and Noémie’s (Calamy) new film project, so the title Call My Agent! The Movie works on more than one level.

So now, silver fox smoothie Mathias (Thibault de Montalembert) is running a small agency with his daughter Camille (Fanny Sidney) while Mathias and his secretary-lover Noémie are finally officially together. Noémie, always a natural organiser, has become a producer with her own hit TV show that looks suspiciously just like Call My Agent! Thanks to complicated (and mostly backfiring) machinations on Mathias’s part, Noémie ends up producing their former colleague Andréa’s first feature as a writer-director.
points: The screwball French comedy is back as a film that actually works, thanks to putting Andréa and Noémie at the heart of chaotic events and bringing all the old faces back.

articles.title: Beehiiv Expands Roster of Creators With Dana Harris-Bridson, David Covucci and Peter Greenberg
articles.summary: Beehiiv, the creator platform that has gained traction through associations with independent journalists such as Oliver Darcy and Joanna Stern, unveiled an expansion of its Media Collective, a roster of journalists who have turned to the company to help launch new digital efforts.
body: “We started the Media Collective to solve a problem I kept hearing from journalists: they wanted to bet on themselves, but going independent meant losing the support system they had spent their careers relying on,” said Tyler Denk, co-founder and CEO of Beehiiv, in a statement. “The Media Collective gives them the scaffolding to build something of their own while staying focused on what they do best: reporting. It’s grown faster and been more successful than we anticipated.”

Greenberg will on September 15 launch “The Upgrade,” reporting on things of key interest to travelers, including airline and hotel practices, cruise ship safety, loyalty programs, travel disruptions and the oversight of aircraft maintenance and airworthiness. Greenberg hosts and produces three long-running television programs: “The Royal Tour,” “Hidden,” and “The Travel Detective.”

Harris-Bridson will launch Flamingo Media in January, 2027. Flamingo will cover what Harris-Bridson calls the “Story Economy,” the increasingly interconnected market spanning entertainment, creators, brands, platforms, technology and capital.

articles.title: Inglourious baristas: why is Brad Pitt making coffee for 16 abusive dogs?
articles.summary: In new film The Heart of the Beast, the A-lister’s bond with his loyal mutt proves crucial. In Spike Jonze’s new advert, Pitt is rather more subservient. Brad Pitt has a new movie out this month, The Heart of the Beast, about an emotionally damaged man who forms a life-saving bond with a dog.
body: But perhaps Brad Pitt knows that getting people to see something as unimaginative as The Heart of the Beast is an uphill struggle, because that would explain why he has just made an advert that looks and feels much more like the Brad Pitt dog movie that deserves to be made. In short, it is an advert where Brad Pitt gets loudly disparaged by a number of dogs for an extended period of time.

As reported by Variety, the commercial is for the De’Longhi Magnifica Duo, an all-singing, all-dancing coffee machine that retails in the UK for about £700. But really the product is beside the point. The main point is that the advert, running to almost two minutes, sees Brad Pitt stumble around cluelessly while a small army of real dogs – all of whom have names, some of whom are dressed in human clothes – shout insults at him.

articles.title: Blue Film review – polarising sex worker drama is well-acted and deeply disturbing
articles.summary: A camboy meets up with a convicted paedophile who turns out to be his old English teacher in Elliot Tuttle’s uncomfortable drama. There have reportedly been audience walk-outs at screenings of this indie drama from young American film-maker Elliot Tuttle, a two-hander about a sex worker hired for…
body: Kieron Moore plays Aaron Eagle (not his real name), a Los Angeles sex worker and camboy. In the video content he livestreams, Aaron is a dom; gym-perfected and tattooed, he hurls homophobic insults at his fans. One night, he arranges to meet a client who offers to pay $50,000 for one night. The retirement-age man who answers the door of the Airbnb turns out to be Aaron’s former English teacher Mr Grant (Reed Birney), who was sacked after attempting to rape a 12-year-old pupil. Aaron was not the victim, but the teacher says he has always been in love with Aaron – though he is no longer sexually attracted to him.

body: The environmental group will recognize the “Wicked” star and his wife Emilie as well as Martha Stewart at its New York gala on Sept. 15.

“It’ll get your blood going and put you on alert,” he recalls. “It’s a fun, exciting, creatively chaotic and delicious week. It seems they’re following something of the same schedule this week. I kind of remember it in my bones. When you finally get yourself out there, you’re trying to just do the assignment. It’s a blast.”

Just three days after “SNL,” Goldblum and Emilie will be honored at Oceana’s annual New York gala at the Rainbow Room at Rockefeller Center on Sept. 15 for their work over the last almost 20 years championing the organization and its work to protect the world’s oceans. Martha Stewart will be named this year’s Ocean Champion. Sam Waterston, an Ocean Board member, will serve as master of ceremonies. The evening will mark Oceana’s 25th anniversary.

Goldblum was first introduced to Oceana through his manager Keith Attis, who is a longtime environmental activist. The Goldblums’ love of the water even inspired their sons’ names, Charlie Ocean, 11 and River Joe, 9.

articles.title: Halloween Film Festival Launched by Ripcord; Indie Platform Aims to Connect Filmmakers With Genre Fans (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Ripcord, a new independent film platform that aims to directly connect genre filmmakers with fans, has announced a spooky new film festival. The Halloween Film Festival is set to showcase 50 short genre films, including horror, sci-fi, thriller and fantasy titles and fans can vote on their…
body: The festival is the launch event for Ripcord, which is described per the company’s official release as “built to close one of independent cinema’s biggest gaps: exceptional films that struggle to find distribution and audiences who struggle to discover them. Rather than relying on traditional distributors, Ripcord lets filmmakers bring their work directly to fans. On Ripcord, fans can discover new creators, follow and interact with the filmmakers behind the films they love and purchase films directly to support them.”

“Too many great independent films never find an audience, not because they aren’t good enough, but because the traditional path to distribution shuts most filmmakers out entirely,” Charlie Cleveland, the founder of Ripcord, said in a statement. “Ripcord exists to remove that gatekeeper and provide filmmakers with a direct line to the fans who are hungry for their work, and give those fans a real hand in discovering what’s next. This festival is the first step in building that home.”

articles.title: Actor Noel Clarke charged with sexual offences
articles.summary: Clarke has been charged with offences including sexual assault. BBC News has asked him for a comment.
body: Actor Noel Clarke has been charged with sexual offences including sexual assault, voyeurism and exposure.
The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) authorised the Metropolitan Police to charge the Doctor Who and Kidulthood star on Wednesday.

Clarke, 50, from Kensington, west London, was charged with two counts of sexual assault, three charges of voyeurism and one charge of exposure. The offences are alleged to have taken place between 2007 and 2016 and relate to five women.

In a statement released on Wednesday, the CPS said: "Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court and that it is in the public interest to do so."

articles.title: Channel 4 to cut 340 jobs by the end of the year in major shake-up
articles.summary: It comes after the network conducted a review amid a "rapidly changing media landscape".
body: Channel 4 has said it plans to cut 340 jobs before the end of the year, reducing its workforce by more than a quarter.
The network, which broadcasts Gogglebox and The Great British Bake Off, will lose around 28% of its current 1,270 staff following a strategic review of the organisation.

Priya Dogra, Channel 4's chief executive, said the announcement "marks the first phase of our transformation, ensuring Channel 4 is the right shape and size to deliver its future strategy and focus investment in the programmes audiences love".
Caroline Dinenage, chair of the culture, media and sport committee said the news would be "deeply worrying for the talented and dedicated people who work at Channel 4".

articles.title: Telluride 2026: Illusion of an Everlasting Summer, Burgundy, Rehearsals for a Revolution
articles.summary: In its 53rd edition, the Telluride Film Festival continues to be an industry leader in exhibiting strong, technically excellent stories. While its documentary slate gained a copious amount of attention because of the world premiere of the secret A24 documentary, “You Can See Everything,” there are…
body: “Illusion of an Everlasting Summer” sounds like an idyllic, beachy CD one’s parents would play in the car with the windows down. This nod to nostalgia is exactly the lens director Alessandra Sanguinetti wants us to look through to see her new documentary. Better known for her photography, Sanguinetti expands and personalizes her practice in piecing together footage captured across 25 years.

Beginning in the late 1990s, “Illusion of an Everlasting Summer” introduces its two main subjects, Guillermina and Belinda, cousins and soulmates. The camcorder quality also contributes to the film’s desire for the past. The grainy home video texture adds more innocence to the curiosity exhibited by the young girls’ play. Their life in rural Argentina is filled with the company of one another, and although they’re conscious they’re being recorded, it does not appear to inhibit their actions.
